The degree counts in Fig. 1d show k = 4 nodes making up 4.6–17.7% of branch points across the six datasets. The pooled 16.6% is 96% human-neuron nodes. Bifurcation angles also fail to peak at 2π/3. | [LIT-099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-099.md) v2 | Framing Effects in Object Perception | Ivy & Mroczko-Wąsowicz (2025), DOI-10.1007/s13164-024-00763-8. A conceptual proposal with no new data. | [LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md) v3 | Mental causation via neuroprosthetics? A critical analysis | Pernu (2018), DOI-10.1007/s11229-018-1713-z. The interventionist/difference-making case for nonreductive mental causation from BCIs (List & Menzies 2009; Menzies 2015; Woodward 2008a,b, 2017) misplaces multiple realisation. What the ensemble recordings show is that one cortical-level variable N (the ensemble's average firing) is realised by many single-neuron patterns N1, N2. Each intention M corresponds to one value of N. So the counterfactual contrast "∼M □→ ∼B true, ∼N □→ ∼B false" fails, and neuroprosthetics supports mental causation only by identifying M with N, not nonreductive physicalism. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-091.md)); Worth reading as a short, precise diagnosis of a specific equivocation in the interventionist BCI argument (multiple realisation at the wrong level). Its scope is limited to difference-making with a proportionality constraint (fn 1), and its identity conclusion rests on a simplified picture of neural decoding that it asserts rather than argues. |

| [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md) | Duality of Bures and Shape Distances with Implications for Comparing Neural Representations | Harvey et al. (2023), [ARXIV-2311.11436](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.11436). The Procrustes shape distance between two representations (optimal rotational alignment of units) equals the Bures distance between their centred linear kernel matrices, so the rotation-invariant geometry of a representation is exactly the geometry of its kernel, and through Uhlmann's theorem the fidelity of two kernels is the maximum overlap over all representations consistent with them. | Deferred — seeded from the abstract and a skim on 2026-09-26; not read in full |

| [LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md) v2 | Attention Approximates Sparse Distributed Memory | Bricken & Pehlevan (2021), [ARXIV-2111.05498](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.05498). Kanerva's SDM read weights each stored pointer by the number of neurons in the intersection of two Hamming balls of radius d. The paper shows that this weight is roughly log-linear in Hamming distance for close patterns. As a result, with L²-normalised vectors and a regression-fitted β, softmax attention reproduces SDM's retrieval behaviour on random and learnt-projection data (App. B.7). Two things are weaker than they look. The analytic derivation (App. B.2, Eqs. 16–21) gets the exponent wrong: by my recomputation its β is ≈2–2.5× too small. The biological case is Kanerva's 1988 cerebellar mapping, restated rather than re-argued. It also needs r = 2⁶⁴ ≈ 1.8×10¹⁹ neurons in the Attention setting, which the paper itself calls "biologically implausible" (App. B.5). | Active — read in full 2026-09-27 (NOTE-242); worth reading as the clearest statement of the SDM–attention correspondence. Its exact circle-intersection formula and its eight-algorithm convergence comparison are the parts to take away. Treat its analytic exponential derivation, its GPT-2 "confirmation" and its cerebellar implementation of attention as argument, not demonstration. |
| [LIT-368](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-368.md) v2 | A decision-making theory of visual detection | Tanner & Swets (1954), DOI-10.1037/h0058700. Tanner and Swets model visual detection as testing a statistical hypothesis. The observer compares one sample of neural activity with a cutoff, and signal+noise and noise are Gaussian with equal variance, separated by d′ (the mean difference in noise-SD units, defined as the square root of Peterson and Birdsall's d). The cutoff moves along a curve of P_SN(A) against P_N(A) (the curve now called the ROC; for d′ = 1 it passes through (.16, .50), (.50, .84) and (.84, .98)). The optimal operating point is where the slope equals β = [(1−P(SN))/P(SN)]·[(V_N·CA+K_N·A)/(V_SN·A+K_SN·CA)]. The 4AFC prediction is P(C)=∫F(x)³g(x)dx. With three paid observers, d′ estimated from yes-no data predicted 4AFC accuracy. The "false alarms are guesses" (high-threshold) hypothesis is rejected: false-alarm rate correlated with chance-corrected thresholds (ρ = .30, .71, .67; combined p ≪ .001), and all 12 fitted yes-no scatter lines miss the point (1, 1). | Active — read in full 2026-09-30 ([NOTE-316](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-316.md)); worth reading as the founding psychophysics paper of signal detection theory: it is short, it is the first place d′ is named, and it is the first to put the observer on the ROC and to set the likelihood-ratio criterion β from priors and payoffs. For the ideal-observer mathematics it defers entirely to Peterson and Birdsall (1953), and its experiment is small (three observers) with some statistics asserted rather than shown. |
| [LIT-373](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-373.md) v4 | The two dragons of cognition: recursive condensation for predictive processing | Li (2026), DOI-10.3389/fncom.2026.1778902. A "Hypothesis and Theory" essay proposing that the neocortex is a "biological Savitch machine". Alternating expansion ("odd parity") and contraction ("even parity") phases manufacture the disjoint closed sets of Urysohn's Lemma, and storing ("memoizing") the condensed tokens converts exponential search into polynomial "navigation". Its one non-standard formal result, Theorem 2, R(N) ∝ b^{αN} (§5.2.2, p. 11), is stated without proof. There is no data, simulation or model. The two mathematical pillars are misdescribed: Savitch's theorem saves space at the cost of time and does not memoize, and Urysohn's Lemma gives a continuous separator, not a linear one, and is not an "if and only if". | Rejected — re-read jointly with [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) and arXiv 2602.07974 on 2026-10-01 ([NOTE-321](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-321.md)); Read jointly with [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) and the companion StrLT preprint (arXiv 2602.07974), the essay is the cognitive motivation of a coherent programme: structure is discovered by costly search, condensed into frozen tokens, and reused cheaply. It is not just a misuse of two theorems. Read charitably, its mathematical slips are repairable and are not the reason to set it aside: the Urysohn "iff" and linear readout, Savitch as memoisation, the Definition 2 clash. The reason is what is left after repair: an amortised-inference and complementary-learning-systems picture already in the literature it cites; a neural mapping whose predictions do not discriminate it from standard consolidation accounts; one original quantitative claim, Theorem 2, that is not argued. A reader who wants the programme should read [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) and the companion, where it is made precise. |
